newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends flat after trading very narrow range.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends flat after trading very narrow range.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended a directionless session a fraction above its opening level, after trading a six-point range.
By 5.50 p.m. (0550 GMT) the kiwi was at US$0.6892/99, against its 0.6889/96 open and 0.6885/90 close on Tuesday.

On its Trade-Weighted Index the kiwi traded down to 67.45 as the dollar/yen weakened, but that cross soon rebounded, which brought the TWI back up to 67.57 (against its 67.55 open and 67.71 close on Tuesday).
Dealers said the kiwi traded a range of US$0.6888-95.
"The only reason it got up to 0.6895 was the Aussie looked very bid in the morning -- it was paid as high as US$0.7520 -- but that soon came off, as did the kiwi, and that was it.
"There has been no local interest, and anything we've seen out of Asia has been small and two-way, so there was nothing of note really," one dealer said.
He said the last few days had seen the kiwi reasonably well bid overnight through the London, European and New York sessions, only to sell back down as the local open neared.
"If that's anything to go by, maybe tonight we'll see it crawl back up to 0.6900 or 0.6905. But overnight I wouldn't see anything outside of 0.6885-05."
